analysis.title: October 2026: First Look on Hedge Fund Performance and Positioning
key_insights: Global Fundamental L/S asset-weighted returns were -3.49% in October vs MSCI TR -0.77%, driven by both beta losses and negative alpha. YTD return is +9.1%.

Systematic L/S returned -3.6% in October, the worst monthly drawdown since November 2020 and the first down month since July 2025. The loss came entirely from negative long-side alpha. YTD return is +16.2%.
October was the first month on the desk's record (since 2016) in which both Fundamental L/S (-3.5%) and Systematic L/S (-3.6%) fell by 3% or more.

Fundamental L/S alpha excluding beta was -1.75%, the worst monthly alpha since July and the second worst in more than four years. Long-side losses were the main driver and short-side losses contributed to a lesser extent.
The largest Fundamental L/S alpha detractors were Volatility, China, Short-Term Momentum and Short Crowdedness. Gains from the United States, Health Care and Size partly offset them.
Systematic L/S alpha detractors were Short Crowdedness, Medium-Term Momentum and Asset Selection. Profitability, Earnings Yield and Growth partly offset them.
Asia L/S managers fell -9.4% in October, US L/S -1.9% and Europe L/S -0.5%. YTD returns are Asia +14%, Europe +7.8% and US +6.4%.
TMT L/S funds lost -12.6% in October (now +5.1% YTD). Health Care L/S funds lost -1.4% (now +8.5% YTD).
The equal-weighted average Fundamental L/S return was -0.98% and the median was -1.69%, against the asset-weighted -3.49%, which suggests large managers underperformed.

Global equities saw the largest dollar net selling since March, with short and long sales roughly equal. Single stocks were net sold on risk unwinds, with long sales outpacing short sales 4 to 1. Index and ETF products were net bought (long buys outpaced short sales 1.6 to 1).
Info Tech, Industrials and Materials were the most net sold global sectors. Consumer Discretionary, Real Estate and Health Care were the most net bought.

US-listed ETF shorts rose 3% in October. ETF shorts are 10.5% of the US equity short book excluding index products (10.1% in September), in the 18th percentile vs the past year and the 1st percentile vs the past five years.

Overall Prime Book gross leverage rose 4.8 pts to 314.5% (86th percentile, 1-year) and net leverage fell 4.2 pts to 73.4% (9th percentile). The long/short ratio fell 3.6% to 1.609 (7th percentile). The desk says the gross increase was driven by mark-to-market.
Global Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 3.2 pts to 49.2% (3rd percentile, 1-year), led by reductions from Asia L/S funds. Gross leverage rose 4.2 pts to 210.7%.
US Fundamental L/S gross leverage rose 6.2 pts to 214.9% and net leverage rose 1.4 pts to 47.1% (8th percentile, 1-year). Asia Fundamental L/S net leverage fell 21.6 pts to 40.9%.
North America was net sold for a second straight month, with short sales outpacing long buys 3.5 to 1. Its weight vs MSCI World ACWI rose 2.1 pts to 15.2% underweight.
Europe was slightly net sold, and the dollar de-grossing was the largest since July. Europe's weight rose 0.7 pts to 3.5% overweight, a 1-year high.

DM Asia was modestly net bought, with short covers outpacing long sales 4.2 to 1. Australia was bought and Japan was sold. EM Asia had the largest dollar net selling since July (long and short sales 2.5 to 1), with Taiwan, Korea and China all net sold.

US TMT was significantly net sold. Info Tech saw the largest dollar net selling since June (long sales vs short sales 4.5 to 1), led by Tech Hardware, Semis & Semi Equipment and IT Services. Software was the only Info Tech subsector not net sold. The US Info Tech long/short ratio is 1.71 (7th percentile vs five years).
US Comm Svcs was net sold for the first time in 4 months. The US Comm Svcs long/short ratio is 2.73 (5th percentile vs the past year).
US Materials saw the largest dollar net selling since May 2024. The US Materials long/short ratio is 1.77 (1st percentile vs five years).

Defensive sectors were net bought for the first time in 7 months. US Health Care was net bought for the first time in 3 months, driven by short covering (1.5 to 1). The US Health Care long/short ratio is 2.40.
risk_factors: Both beta and alpha losses hit Fundamental L/S managers, and the worst alpha in more than four years excluding July suggests stock-selection risk, led by long-side losses.
Short crowdedness was a drag on both cohorts, indicating risk in crowded shorts.
Large managers underperformed smaller ones (weighted average -3.49% vs median -1.69%).
Net leverage is at multi-year lows for several cohorts while gross leverage is elevated, so positioning is defensive but gross exposure is exposed to mark-to-market moves.
vol_and_positioning: Global Fundamental L/S net leverage is 49.2%, in the 3rd percentile of the past year and the 5th percentile of the past three years.
Overall Prime Book net leverage is 73.4% (9th percentile, 1-year) while gross leverage is 314.5% (86th percentile, 1-year, 97th percentile, 5-year).
Overall Prime Book long/short ratio is 1.609, in the 2nd percentile vs five years. Global Fundamental L/S long/short ratio is 1.610 (3rd percentile, 1-year).
Short Crowdedness was a top alpha detractor for both Fundamental and Systematic L/S in October.
ETF shorts are 10.5% of the US equity short book excluding index products, in the 1st percentile vs the past five years.

US Info Tech long/short ratio is 1.71 (20th percentile, 1-year). US Consumer Discretionary is 2.01 (4th percentile, 1-year). US Materials is 1.77 (3rd percentile, 1-year). US Comm Svcs is 2.73 (5th percentile, 1-year). US Health Care is 2.40 (6th percentile, 1-year).
Hedge funds rotated out of TMT and Cyclicals and into Defensives in October.
